title: Fingerprint checks
blurb: Measure what a page inside a profile can see, score it against the declared identity, and tag the leakers.
instructions:
You are now running fingerprint checks: a page opened inside the profile
reports what it can see, and Argus scores that against the identity it
declared for that profile. One profile is one call and a sentence back.
Many profiles is a sweep, and the order below is the whole skill --
nothing works in any other order.

## The dataset comes first -- hard rule

For a sweep the control structure is created in the Data tab BEFORE
anything is measured: one row per profile, and the per-profile values live
in ROWS, never hard-coded into your prose or into a step. The columns:

- Profile -- type 'Profile', the profile the row is about.
- Score -- type 'Number', 0-100.
- Verdict -- type 'Status (one choice)' with exactly three chip options:
  coherent, issues, leaking. Do not invent a fourth; the scorer emits
  these three and a chip the scorer never writes is a filter that always
  comes back empty.
- Failed checks -- type 'Text', the ids that did not pass (webrtc,
  timezone, platform...), comma separated.
- Checked at -- type 'Date and time'.

list_profiles for the scope, then list_datasets to find the dataset. If it
does not exist, create_dataset makes it and add_rows seeds one row per
profile; if it does, sample_rows first to confirm the shape before
touching anything. A row that landed wrong is fixed with update_rows IN
PLACE -- never by re-adding a copy, which is how a sweep of 40 profiles
turns into 80 rows and a verdict count nobody can trust.

## One check call per profile -- never an automation

The per-profile step is a single fingerprint check call:
argus_fingerprint_check over MCP, POST /v1/profiles/fingerprint-check over
the local API. Never an authored automation that re-implements the probes
as evaluate steps.

Two reasons, and both are the point of this skill. One engine means the
in-app panel and your sweep can never report two different verdicts for
the same profile. And the boundary sentence below gets written once, in
one place, instead of being re-derived by whoever reads your steps. If you
find yourself calling create_automation here, stop: you are building a
second engine that will drift from the first.

Take profiles one at a time and write each result to its row before
starting the next. A batch of calls fired at once means several profiles
opening a check tab in the same second, and a failure mid-batch leaves you
unable to say which rows are current.

## The profile must be open with a debugging port

The check attaches to a running window; it cannot conjure one.

- Profile not open: the call answers notRunning. That is NOT a verdict.
  Do not write 'leaking', 'issues' or a zero score into the row for it --
  launch_profile first (the user approves the launch), let the window
  settle, then check. If the user does not want it launched, leave the row
  untouched and say which profiles were skipped.
- Window open but launched with no debugging port: the call answers
  noPort. Argus opens that port only when the workspace has an automation
  the browser could be asked to run -- pinned to the profile's start page,
  attached to the profile, or merely present in the workspace for the
  Argus Helper panel to offer. An always-on port would itself be an
  anti-detect regression, so this is a state to explain, not a bug to work
  around: the fix is to close the window and launch again from Argus.

Read troubleshooting/fingerprint-check before you explain either state, so
the words you use match the ones the panel uses.

## The network option is off by default -- leave it there

By default the check makes NO outbound request at all: the probes run on a
local file:// page and nothing leaves the machine. That is what stops the
check from being the leak it is looking for.

Ticking the network option adds two things per profile: a STUN lookup and
one request to an IP echo, both from that profile's own identity. Over a
batch that is one outbound request per profile, from a different exit each
time. Never tick it for a whole batch without saying so first, in the same
message that asks to run the batch, and never leave it on for the next
sweep by habit.

Without it the egress and webrtc_srflx checks report as 'skip'. A skip is
a measurement that did not happen -- report it as that, never as a pass.

## What a pass means, and what it does not

Argus cannot verify the browser's spoofing internals. The check measures
what a page inside the profile can SEE, and compares that against what
Argus declared for the profile. A pass means the page-visible identity is
coherent with the declared identity -- not that the anti-detect engine
works, and not that the profile is undetectable.

Say that in your own words every time you report a score. A user who
hears 'undetectable' from a 100 is the exact failure this skill exists to
prevent. read_doc concepts/fingerprint-check for what each check compares
and what it cannot reach.

## Verdict -> what to do

- coherent -- nothing contradicted the declared identity. Report the
  score, the boundary sentence, and stop.
- issues -- something the page sees disagrees with what Argus declared:
  timezone, language, user_agent, platform, screen, hardware,
  webgl_strings, do_not_track. These are fingerprint fields, so the fix
  lives in the profile editor: open_profile_editor with section
  'fingerprint' (Edit fingerprint). Say which field and what it should
  become. Two of them are not fixable and must not be reported as if they
  were -- an Android or iOS preset reports a desktop platform because
  those presets set a user-agent string and no client-hints override, and
  a first noise hash has nothing to compare against yet.
- leaking -- the real machine or the real exit is visible to the page:
  webrtc, webrtc_srflx, egress. These are proxy-shaped, not
  fingerprint-shaped. check_proxy re-measures the assigned proxy,
  list_proxies shows what else is available, and go_to_tab 'proxies' puts
  the user in front of the library. Assigning a different proxy is a
  SEPARATE explicit step the user agrees to (assign_profile_proxy), never
  something you do because a score was low.
- The datacenter check is a warning about the proxy's exit network, not a
  leak: a hosting exit is low-anonymity, and the answer is a residential
  proxy, not a fingerprint edit. concepts/proxies-udp-quic explains why a
  proxied profile emits no non-proxied UDP in the first place.

## Close the loop downstream

The sweep writes; the reading comes after, in order. AFTER every profile
has been checked -- never while the Verdict column is still mid-flight --
query_rows the dataset for verdict = 'leaking' and tag those profiles with
update_profile_fields (batch: the profile_ids array, one call).

Two things about tags, both of which silently destroy work if you miss
them. The tags argument REPLACES a profile's tag list, so read the
profile's current tags with get_profile or list_profiles and send those
plus the new one -- sending one tag wipes the other four. And a profile
holds at most five tags: extras are dropped without an error, so a profile
already carrying five keeps the five it has and your tag never lands. Say
so rather than reporting a tag you did not apply.

## Planning

A full sweep has several parts in a fixed order: the dataset, the launches
for anything not running, the checks one profile at a time, then the
downstream tagging. When the user wants the whole loop at once, plan it
with make_plan so the order -- and whether the network option is on -- is
agreed before the first window opens.
